title: Unit – 4 : Session – 11 : SLO – 2  |  B-Trees — Deletion Algorithm
sections: I. Deleting a Leaf Node Value
Deletion is also done from the LEAF NODES. Two cases: a LEAF NODE value has to be deleted,
or an INTERNAL NODE value has to be deleted.
Step 1: Locate the LEAF NODE which has to be deleted.
Step 2: If the leaf node contains MORE THAN the minimum number of key values (more than m/2 elements),
Step 3: Else fill the node by taking an element either from the LEFT sibling or from the RIGHT sibling.
a) If the left sibling has more than the MINIMUM NUMBER of key values, push its largest key into
its PARENT NODE and pull down the INTERVENING ELEMENT from the parent node to the leaf node.
b) Else, if the right sibling has more than the minimum number of key values, push its SMALLEST KEY
into its parent node and pull down the intervening element to the LEAF NODE where the key is deleted.
c) Else, MERGE a new leaf node by combining the TWO SIBLINGS (leaf + sibling) and the intervening
element of the parent node. If pulling the intervening element leaves the parent with less than the
minimum number of keys, then PROPAGATE (repeat) the process upwards, thereby REDUCING the height
II. Deleting an Internal Node Value
To delete an internal node, promote the INORDER PREDECESSOR OR INORDER SUCCESSOR of the key to be
deleted to occupy the position of the deleted key. This predecessor or successor will always be in a
LEAF NODE. So the processing is done as if a value from the leaf node has been deleted.
